report.body:
Police acted on an anonymous tip that a man was selling drugs from a white VW
Gol in the Jardim das Palmeiras neighbourhood of Água Clara, in Mato Grosso do
Sul. Military Police officers located the car, the driver tried to flee
when he saw the patrol and was caught after a chase of a few blocks. The
driver, a 30-year-old man already under investigation by the Civil Police's
Seção de Investigações Gerais (SIG), was arrested, and officers found a portion
of substance resembling cocaine in the car. At his home, officers seized
portions of marijuana and a precision scale.

Information from the stop led investigators to a second address used to store
drugs, where they found 59 tablets of marijuana weighing about 54 kilograms and
arrested two men aged 18 and 20. The first reports of the operation said a
joint task force had located two more suspects at a snack bar and then found the
59 tablets, weighing about 54 kilograms. A fourth suspect, aged 22, was
detained with about 500 grams of marijuana and a precision scale. The fifth
man, aged 28, was already investigated for drug trafficking and was captured on
an open arrest warrant. About 54.5 kilograms of marijuana were seized in
total: the roughly 54 kilograms of tablets plus the 500 grams found with the
fourth suspect. A bag with 19 portions of cocaine totalling about 120 grams
was also found, which the Civil Police said the first suspect had discarded
during the Military Police approach.

The Civil Police balance put the seizure at about 54.64 kilograms of marijuana
and cocaine, plus a car, a motorcycle, three precision scales, three mobile
phones, packaging material and about R$250 in cash. Four of the five were
booked in flagrante for drug trafficking and criminal association for
trafficking, and the fifth was captured under a judicial order. The people
involved were taken to the Civil Police station in Água Clara for the legal
procedures. The initial account of the operation placed the drug stash in a
wooded area near the MS-324 highway.

Officers of the Mossos d'Esquadra criminal investigation division arrested seven
men aged between 29 and 55 on 1 October 2026, suspected of links to a
drug-trafficking organisation. The operation took place in an industrial
warehouse in Cabanes (Girona), where officers seized 8,025 kg of hashish.

The Catalan government's press note confirms the 8,025 kilograms of hashish were
seized from the Cabanes warehouse in Alt Empordà.

The arrests are the result of an investigation by the drug squad of the criminal
investigation division in Sant Feliu de Llobregat, which identified a warehouse
used solely for the storage and distribution of drugs.

The hashish was hidden among legal merchandise in a truck trailer, inside large
raffia sacks loaded with rubber granulate to hinder police and customs checks. Police valued the seized substance at more than 16.2 million euros on the
illicit market. During the search, officers also found a firearm in one of
the detainees' vans.

The investigation began in June 2026 after police intercepted a van in
Viladecans (Barcelona) carrying nearly 2,400 kg of hashish, which they traced to
the Cabanes warehouse; Investigating Court No. 7 of Gavà took the case.

The seven detainees were brought before the Investigating Court of Figueres. All seven entered prison on remand: four without bail and the other three
with bail. The investigation remains open and further arrests are not ruled
out.

The seizure is more than half of the roughly 14,900 kg of hashish the Mossos
d'Esquadra had seized in Catalonia by 1 October 2026, and one of the force's
largest operations by volume.

report.title: Driver jailed pending trial over 300 kg Ceuta port hashish haul
report.summary: The trucker arrested by Spain's UDYCO drug unit at the port of Ceuta on 13 November with about 300 kg of hashish hidden in a false bottom was put at judicial disposal on 15 November and remanded in pretrial custody for an offence against public health. The investigation remains open amid suspicions of larger loads and other vehicles with hidden caches.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments.

The hashish was hidden in a false bottom adapted in the rear area of the cab, at the end of the vehicle's cargo area, which was to cross to the boarding zone carrying no load other than the drugs. The false bottom was very well made, so that officers had difficulty reaching the drugs and did not stop until they opened the sheet metal hiding the compartment where the sacks had been concealed. Officers used every means possible, including hammers, bolt cutters, mallets and an angle grinder, until they broke through the false bottom's protection. The truck driver was detained in situ by UDYCO, shown the hashish found, and then transferred to police premises. It was on Sunday 15 November that the driver was put at judicial disposal, with a pretrial detention order issued for an offence against public health. The investigation remains open amid suspicions of larger loads of merchandise and concealment of heavy vehicles in spaces serving as zulos, or hashish storehouses. FAROTV observed the officers' work until they extracted all the sacks with drugs, which were loaded into a police van for transfer and subsequent weighing.

The National Police arrested four men and one woman in Palma as suspected
members of a group dedicated to drug trafficking, seizing 60 kilograms of

Narcotics Group I of the National Police closed an investigation begun months

and intervened the parcel, which contained 24 kilograms of hashish, and arrested

other suspected collaborators and two homes that might hold more drugs, and both
homes were searched.

an air rifle with a silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash, and arrested the
man and a woman there on suspicion of drug trafficking and membership of a
criminal organisation. Ultima Hora reported that the man and woman arrested
in that first home were the main suspect and his partner. At the second
home officers arrested a second suspect said to have been in charge of storing
and transporting the drugs. In that home they found two kilograms of
cocaine, several doses, cutting substance, a pistol with nine-millimetre
cartridges, a bow with arrows and a hydraulic press allegedly used to compress
the cocaine.

A fifth person was arrested for their connection with the case, and police
suspect the drugs were distributed to others for sale on a smaller scale; the
investigation remains open and further arrests are not ruled out. Officers
of the Unidad de Prevención y Reacción, the Grupo II de Estupefacientes and dog

operation's balance as 60 kilograms of hashish, two kilograms of cocaine,

A Ukrainian driver was arrested at Saint-Lary-Soulan, in the Hautes-Pyrénées, on
the evening of Monday 28 September 2026 as he transported more than 32 kilograms
of cannabis herb in his car. On 1 October 2026 the tribunal correctionnel
de Tarbes, the city's criminal court, sentenced him to 24 months in prison and a
ten-year ban from French territory.

Customs officers had stopped his Renault Talisman on a roundabout at
Saint-Lary-Soulan at 10.15 pm. The car was returning from Spain through the
Aragnouet-Bielsa tunnel. The customs administrator for the sector said the
tunnel, like the central Pyrenees, was a route increasingly used by criminal
networks. Under a non-original carpet in the modified floor, officers found
two metal boxes holding 32 heat-sealed bags of cannabis herb, 32.8 kilograms in
all. They also seized rags soaked in white spirit, used to mask the smell
of the drugs, and 405 euros in cash. The customs valued the drugs at
131,200 euros.

The driver was a Ukrainian resident in Poland with no criminal record. He
told the court he had been contacted through the Telegram network by someone he
did not know, and said he was paid 3,000 euros to collect the drugs in Alicante
and take them to Poland. Tarbes Infos reported he said he did not know the
organisers of the traffic and acted out of financial need to support his family,
expressing regret before the tribunal. The conviction covered transporting
narcotics without regular supporting documents and customs money laundering. The customs fines came to 131,605 euros in total. The court also
ordered the confiscation of the 32.8 kg of cannabis, the 405 euros in cash in
50, 20 and 5 euro notes, two telephones and a computer. He was taken into
custody under a committal order for the two-year term, and a sentence adjustment
in the form of conditional release with expulsion was proposed to him. At
the hearing the judge told him he could 'be more useful to his country on his
return' rather than practising smuggling in France.

report.summary: Gendarmerie JASAT teams raided eight addresses in Mustafakemalpaşa, Bursa, on 11 November 2026 and caught 17 suspects in the 2010 murder of construction worker Mehmet Arıcan, shot dead with a hunting rifle. report.body:
Gendarmerie crime-investigation teams known as Jasat carried out simultaneous
raids on eight addresses in Mustafakemalpaşa on 11 November 2026 and caught 17
suspects in the 2010 murder case of construction worker Mehmet Arıcan.
Arıcan disappeared after leaving work in the district's Taşpınar neighbourhood
on 7 September 2010, and his body was found four days later in the Karanlıkdere
area. An examination established that Arıcan had been shot dead with a
hunting rifle in a forest. One of the 17 suspects taken into custody, H.F.,
was remanded in custody by the court he was brought before, and the other 16
were released.

The investigation determined that the murder was committed as a result of
hostility arising from unauthorised entry into a cannabis field. At the
time of the killing there was a feud between Mehmet Arıcan and H.F. over the
unauthorised entry into the cannabis field.

The first investigation had included Hüseyin F., Z.F. and H.Y. in the file as
suspects, but the case was shelved in permanent search after a decision of no
prosecution. In the reopened investigation HTS analyses were carried out on
the 22 GSM lines of 10 suspects. A person who wanted to give secret-witness
testimony gave a statement at the Mustafakemalpaşa chief public prosecutor's
office.

The Bursa Provincial Gendarmerie Command's Jandarma Suç Araştırma Timi (JASAT),
the gendarmerie's crime-investigation teams, carried out the work on the
unsolved killing. Nine gendarmerie public-order teams, five JASAT teams,
one gendarmerie special-operations team and two detector dogs took part in the
operation. The gendarmerie account says the 16 other suspects were released
after their statements were taken, while Hüseyin F., identified as the killer,
was remanded and taken to Bursa E Type Closed Prison. The gendarmerie
account says strong suspicion emerged that eight other named men helped the
suspected killer flee and hide. Justice Minister Akın Gürlek announced that
two unsolved murders in Bursa and one in Tatvan, Bitlis, had been solved and
thanked the teams involved.
